evals.prompt: Maple Valley Hospice Foundation ($2.3M, Vermont) has two fundraisers and a part-time data person. Donor data lives in Excel, an old DonorPerfect instance nobody fully trusts, and Mailchimp. Several board members want us to 'just buy Salesforce.' Help us pick a new CRM.
evals.expected_output: Frames the decision by tier fit, provides a weighted comparison matrix staff complete themselves with 3-year TCO and export rights, and runs discovery with development staff, verifying vendor details.
assertions: Matches the organization to a CRM tier based on size and staffing before comparing features, addressing whether an enterprise system needing an admin fits
Provides a weighted comparison matrix that staff score themselves
Includes 3-year total cost of ownership covering license, implementation, migration and training
Includes data ownership and full export rights as a criterion
Recommends discovery that interviews the staff who touch donor data and looks for shadow spreadsheets
Tells the user to verify current vendor products and pricing

evals.prompt: migrating ~9k records next month from spreadsheets + old system. spouses are separate rows, matching gifts were entered as regular gifts. how do i not screw this up
evals.expected_output: A pre-migration plan: record standard with households, field map, explicit soft-credit logic, and an audited test migration.
assertions: Defines a constituent record standard including households (one record per person, not per gift)
Builds a field map and parks unmapped fields in custom fields rather than dropping data
Sets explicit soft-credit logic so spouse and matching gifts are not posted as duplicate hard credits
Recommends a test migration on a subset audited by two staff against source records
Picks a single source of truth per field when merging systems

evals.prompt: Our CRM is full of duplicates and our gala invitation went to the same household three times. Can you fix our data process and also write our year-end appeal with ask strings for each segment?
evals.expected_output: Sets up ongoing dedup, a data entry policy, a named CRM steward and NCOA, and hands the appeal copy and ask strings to the annual appeals skill.
assertions: Recommends a dedup pass at least quarterly using the CRM's native or marketplace dedup tool
Recommends a written data entry policy with required fields and naming conventions
Recommends assigning a named CRM steward responsible for hygiene
Recommends NCOA or address updates before major mailings
Hands the appeal copy and ask strings to nonprofit-annual-appeals

should_not_trigger.query: Write ask strings for our lapsed-donor spring appeal
Set up a Classy peer-to-peer page for our 5K
